title: Commercial Lead - Clinical Trials
description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role 

We are hiring a Clinical Trials Lead to own the commercial work that follows. You will develop Heidi’s view of the market, identify the strongest entry point, build senior relationships across the industry, secure early customers and shape a repeatable route to market. Your knowledge of clinical trials will inform and shape what Heidi builds.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who operates like a founder. You will make the calls, open the doors, write the proposal, run the meeting and stay accountable after the contract is signed. As the business proves itself, the role can grow into broader ownership of Heidi’s clinical trials business.

What you’ll do 

- Develop the market thesis. Map the clinical trials ecosystem, test the most valuable opportunities and recommend where Heidi should focus its time and capital.

- Lead customer development. Build direct relationships with senior decision makers across sponsors, biotechnology companies, CROs, sites and health systems. Conduct the outreach yourself and turn conversations into qualified opportunities.

- Own early commercial outcomes. Build the pipeline, secure design partners and paid programmes, and own early revenue. Define the measures that show whether the business is gaining traction.

- Shape the proposition. Turn buyer needs into a clear commercial offer, including target customer, value proposition, pricing, packaging and proof of value.

- Inform what Heidi builds. Bring evidence from customers and clinical trials workflows to the product lead. Help the team choose problems worth solving while the product lead retains ownership of product strategy and delivery.

- Navigate the buying process. Understand how life sciences organisations evaluate vendors, allocate budgets, manage procurement and compliance, and move from pilot to broader deployment.

- Build the delivery model. Work with product, engineering, clinical, legal and implementation colleagues to make early programmes successful and increasingly repeatable.

- Create the route to scale. Determine which partnerships, channels, proof points and team capabilities are required to grow beyond founder-led selling.

- Represent Heidi. Build Heidi’s credibility with customers, partners and industry networks through thoughtful engagement and useful domain expertise.

What you’ll need 

The strongest candidates will combine deep clinical trials knowledge with a record of creating commercial value. We expect the following experience.

- Deep experience in the clinical trials industry through a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company, CRO, trial technology business, research network or closely related organisation.

- A strong understanding of how clinical trials are funded, sold, bought and delivered, including the incentives and constraints faced by sponsors, CROs and research sites.

- A record of building revenue, partnerships, a business line or a company in the sector. You can show what you personally originated and how it performed.

- Senior commercial credibility. You can open a conversation with an industry executive, diagnose the underlying business problem and move the relationship towards a concrete commitment.

- The judgement to operate in a regulated environment while respecting Good Clinical Practice, patient consent, privacy and data integrity.

- The independence to create structure, make decisions and produce results without an established playbook or a large supporting team.

- Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping, or side projects.

- You default to building over requesting.

- You're confident in your thinking and open to being wrong. Great ideas win regardless of who surfaces them.

How we show up 

- Build for the next decade, not next quarter . Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

- Lead, don't wait . We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

- Follow the evidence . Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

- Own the outcome . Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

- Ship, measure, go again . A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

- Live in clinicians' reality . Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi? 

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you. 

We offer comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a £100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a £500 home office budget, a £700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to £7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year, Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub , if you care to take a peek.

About the Role 

Ramp is seeking a 2LoD Compliance Strategist to provide dedicated independent second-line assurance across Ramp UK & Irish regulated businesses.

The role sits within Ramp's Europe Compliance function and supports the Head of Compliance & MLRO - Europe. You will not own first-line operational decisions or perform routine casework. - Provide independent compliance input and advisory on significant product, payments, outsourcing, and operational changes.

- Deputise for the Head of Compliance & MLRO where required.

description:
Help shape the future of robotics in construction. 

ABOUT XYZ REALITY 

XYZ Reality created the world’s first and only engineering-grade augmented reality solution, purpose-built for the construction industry. XYZ has grown to over 150 staff across the UK, US and Europe, and works with mission-critical organisations and construction companies to deliver major projects.

THE ROLE 

Construction sites are some of the hardest environments for robot autonomy: they change every day and are full of clutter, obstacles and people. XYZ Reality’s robotics programme is extending our technology toward robots that can operate reliably in them, from autonomous data collection and construction progress capture through to executing construction tasks.

We’re looking for a Robotics Engineer to make that real. You’ll work hands-on with robot hardware in our London office, using a modern stack (ROS 2, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, learning-based control), and see your work tested in real construction environments, not just in simulation.

This is a hands-on, individual contributor role focused on robot software and algorithmic control, backed by a good working knowledge of robot hardware. If you have strong robotics fundamentals from an MSc, PhD or applied research group, love making systems work on real robots, and want your ideas to shape the direction of a programme, we want to hear from you.

This is an office-based role at our London site in Angel, Islington.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

- Integrate robots with XYZ’s software, bringing up ROS / ROS 2 interfaces, robot control, sensors, compute and data flows, and building repeatable tools for bring-up, configuration, logging and monitoring.

- Establish reliable baseline control and develop task-specific behaviours for navigation, positioning and capture, training and tuning control policies in simulation and validating them on hardware.

- Develop localisation-aware path planning, waypoint execution and obstacle handling, working with project and site teams to turn work plans and BIM-derived locations into robot missions.

- Integrate capture payloads so images, pose, timing and mission status flow reliably into XYZ’s construction progress workflows, working with navigation, SLAM and perception colleagues.

- Design test scenarios and measure mission completion, coverage, localisation quality, intervention, recovery and repeatability, improving the system through measured iterations.

- Bring technical expertise and new ideas to the programme, comparing scripted, motion-planning and learning-based approaches and helping shape what comes next.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

- MSc or PhD in Robotics, Controls, Computer Science, Mechatronics or a related discipline, or equivalent applied robotics experience. Industry experience is not required.

- Hands-on experience building, programming or directly controlling a physical robot, from an academic project, research lab or industry.

- Strong Python and C++, practical ROS experience (ideally ROS 2) and working knowledge of kinematics, coordinate frames, feedback control, state estimation, path planning and robot hardware.

- Experience training or tuning robot control policies (e.g. reinforcement or imitation learning) using NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim or similar tools, with a rigorous experimental approach.

- The right to work in the UK. We’re unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

KEY EXPERIENCE & SKILLS 

- ROS / ROS 2, Python & C++

- Robot control, kinematics, state estimation & path planning

- NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim, reinforcement or imitation learning

- Sim-to-real transfer on physical hardware (desirable)

- Navigation, SLAM, perception & sensor fusion (desirable)

Finance admin and communication 

- Run the invoice inbox, logging, chasing and routing supplier invoices so nothing reaches the ledger without a document

The EU Compute team has a specific focus on provisioning, scaling, and the efficient operation of GPU infrastructure for AI and ML workloads. We're looking for a Staff Engineer to be a hands-on technical leader for this infrastructure work that crosses team and brand boundaries. You'll set direction for the platform, turn complex problems into deliverable plans, write and review production code, and help other engineers make sound decisions. It's an exciting time to join: we're building a global platform and the choices made now will shape how engineers across the company ship for years.

What you'll be doing

You'll own some of the hardest infrastructure problems in the company and make the platform easier to operate and safer to build on. We're determined to build great platform products and user experiences, and you'll be pivotal in making this reality.

Day-to-day in this role you'll:

- Set technical direction for shared AWS and Kubernetes infrastructure, balancing reliability, security, developer experience, and cost.

- Lead substantial initiatives from design through rollout and operation, coordinating dependencies and decisions across Wolt, Deliveroo and DoorDash, focusing on workloads targeting GPUs.

- Evolve Kubernetes clusters, cloud networking, identity, and infrastructure provisioning to support growing and varied workloads.

- Build reusable Terraform patterns and self-service tooling that help teams provision infrastructure safely and consistently.

- Improve deployment and operational practices, including GitOps, observability, capacity planning, incident response and recovery.

- Use production signals and developer feedback to find platform friction, choose where to invest and measure whether changes actually help.

- Assist with supporting the platform, with deep focus on GPU infrastructure, as well as broad focus on compute in general.

- Gracefully sunset legacy infrastructure and tooling, and create strategies to reduce toil.

- Mentor engineers through design reviews, implementation and incidents, raising the quality of infrastructure work across teams.

Our humble expectations

- Deep experience building and operating Kubernetes and AWS infrastructure in production. Familiarity with GPU workloads and orchestration is a plus.

- Strong software engineering skills: you use Go, Python or a similar language to build maintainable tools and automation.

- Experience with infrastructure as code (we use Terraform) and with designing systems that other engineering teams depend on.

- A track record of leading complex technical work across teams, including architectural decisions, delivery, and operational follow-through. You have the breadth to collaborate and design across team and domain boundaries, and the depth to have hands-on impact.

- Strong judgment on trade-offs in distributed systems, networking, security, reliability, and cloud cost.

- Clear communication, and the ability to bring people together around a practical technical direction.

What we offer

- Scope and influence. Shape infrastructure used globally, while staying close to the engineering. Your work will help product teams ship services with greater ease and confidence.

- Real problems at global scale. Multi-cluster Kubernetes, AI / ML workloads, cloud networking, GitOps, and progressive delivery across a global company.

- Autonomy and ownership. Set direction and see it through from design to operation, with the backing of a global engineering organisation spanning Europe and the US.

- Growth. Room to expand your scope, whether through deeper technical leadership or broader cross-domain influence.

- Great people. Work with talented engineers and leaders in a diverse, international environment, mentoring and learning from others.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion 

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

title: Golang Backend Engineer, Financial Product Fraud
description:
Our Global Structure 

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London , UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

- Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.

- Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.

- Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.

- Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.

- Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.

- Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.

- Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.

Our expectations:

- 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.

- 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.

- A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.

- Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).

- Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.

- Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.

Nice to have 

- Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.

- Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.

- Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.

- Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).

- Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes.

What we value 

- A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output.

- Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them.

- A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments.

- Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together.

- An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!

title: Data Privacy Analyst - Regulatory Compliance
description:
The company 

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team 

The Compliance team’s mission is to keep iwoca a safe and trusted lender for UK small businesses, and to make the compliant path the easy path for the teams we work with.

We make sure iwoca meets its regulatory obligations, particularly the financial crime, sanctions and data protection requirements that apply across our suite of products and services.

We are the second line of defence for the UK business. We advise the people building and running the business on what the rules require, set the policies and standards they work to, and test whether what happens in practice matches them. We work alongside the product teams so that each product meets its obligations and can grow.

Data protection is central to what we do. We hold the data privacy function for the UK business and own how iwoca handles personal data end to end: the lawful basis for how customer, applicant and third-party data is used; data subject access requests and other individual rights; personal data breaches; retention and deletion; records of processing; marketing and consent; the privacy review of new products and features; and the governance of automated decisioning and AI tooling.

How we work: 

- We enable rather than block. The answer is rarely just “no” — it’s what it would take to get to yes, and what the firm is accepting if it goes ahead anyway.

- We go to the source. Positions are grounded in the actual rule, regulation or guidance, and we can show where they come from.

- We’re proportionate. Controls match the risk in front of us. We don’t build process for its own sake.

- We’re close to the business. We work directly with Tech, Data, Credit, Operations and Legal, and we want to be in the room early rather than at the end.

The role 

As Data Privacy Analyst you will run iwoca’s day-to-day UK data protection work and help the business apply UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR in practice. Your primary focus will be the statutory core: data subject access requests, data protection impact assessments, legitimate interests assessments, personal data breaches and records of processing.

The role is not only to run that work but to improve it. A significant part of the job is identifying where our privacy operations could be automated, supported by AI or otherwise improved, assessing what each option would take and what it would mean for compliance, and specifying it well enough for our Tech and Data teams to deliver.

There is real room for the role to grow: as you build credibility, so does the scope, towards owning areas of the framework outright, leading on AI and automation governance, and taking a larger advisory remit across the business.

You will report to the Data Privacy Manager and work closely with the Head of Compliance who also acts as iwoca’s DPO, so you will have experienced support on the harder judgement calls. This is a hands-on role and the work is visible — much of it goes to senior stakeholders or to the regulator.

Impact and influence 

- Individual rights and data breaches. Own data subject access requests from intake to response — scoping the search, applying exemptions and meeting the statutory deadline — along with erasure, rectification and objection requests. Triage and investigate suspected personal data breaches, assess them against the 72-hour notification test, and keep the breach register accurate.

- Privacy assessments and advice. Assist with DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments and other privacy reviews on new products, features, suppliers and data flows. Be an accessible first point of contact for teams across iwoca with a data protection question, and give them an answer they can act on, early enough to shape what they build.

- Records, policies and reporting. Keep the record of processing activities accurate as the business changes, hold the retention and deletion schedules to account, review data processing agreements with suppliers, help maintain our data protection policies and standards, and produce the privacy reporting that goes to senior stakeholders.

- AI and automated decisioning. Help assess AI tooling and automated decision-making across lending and operations: what personal data goes in, what lawful basis supports it, what the model does with it, and what rights customers have over the outcome. That includes the risks specific to these systems — decisions taken without meaningful human involvement, bias in outcomes, unreliable model output — and recommending how we address them.

- Automation and improvement. Identify the manual steps in our privacy operations that should not be manual, assess the options, and set out the requirements and compliance implications clearly enough for Tech and Data to deliver them.

The requirements 

Essential skills 

- Experience. Experience in data protection or privacy operations, or in a compliance, legal, risk or operational role where data protection was a real part of the job.

- Data protection knowledge. A solid practical understanding of UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR, and of how the ICO expects firms to apply them. Familiarity with the changes made by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 is an advantage.

- Privacy operations and assessments. Hands-on experience of statutory work: DSARs, DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments, breach handling, ROPA maintenance or data processing agreement review. You may not have done all of these — but we want to see that you have done some of them properly.

- AI and automation. A real interest in, and working understanding of, how data protection law applies to AI and automated decision-making. Enough technical fluency to see where a manual process could be automated, set out what is needed, and hold your own in a conversation with engineers.

- Stakeholder management: Comfortable dealing directly with product, engineering, marketing, credit and operations teams, and able to give a non-specialist a clear answer they can act on rather than a legal summary.

Bonus: 

- Sector experience. Financial services or fintech, ideally in lending or payments.

- Credentials. A privacy or AI qualification such as CIPP/E, CIPM, or ICO-recognised practitioner certificates — or working towards one.

- Practical tooling. Experience using Claude Code, LLMs or privacy management platforms.

The culture 

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices 

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits 

- Flexible working hours.

- Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

- A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

- A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

- 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

- A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

- Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

- 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

- An employee equity incentive scheme.

- Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

- Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

- Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

- A learning and development budget for everyone.

- Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

- Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
About Payflows 

At Payflows, we build software that helps large companies manage and automate their payment workflows. It’s not the flashiest part of a business, but it’s one of the most critical: invoices, approvals, payments, and controls. When these things slow down, the whole company feels it. 

But our ambition goes further than just building a better workflow tool. 

We believe the future of finance operations is not faster clicking: it’s no clicking at all 🫳 🎤 

Finance teams shouldn’t spend their days moving data from one screen to another. Software should do the operational work, and humans should focus on reviewing, approving, and making the decisions that matter. 

That’s the direction we’re building toward: an agent-driven finance platform , where intelligent agents handle the repetitive tasks, and users stay in control. 

We started in 2022 with a small team and a rough first version of the product. Three years later, we’re working with major companies across France, the UK, and the US while choosing to keep our team small and human-sized. 

We moved fast, shipped a lot, and not everything was built in a perfect way. But it helped us learn quickly, sign real customers, and prove that the problem we’re solving truly matters. 

In 2024, investors trusted us with a $25M Series A. That gives us the chance to keep growing while also strengthening our foundations and building the system that will power this agent-driven future. 

Today, we’re about 35 people from many different countries, and we’re looking for a few amazing humans to join the next chapter. 🤗 

🚀 What you’ll actually do 

You’ll help build a product that real finance teams rely on every day. 

For us, engineering is not just about clean code, it’s about reliability, clarity, and trust, especially when money and automation are involved. 

In a typical week, you might: 

- Design and implement new services for a product feature. 

- Refactor an early service to make it more robust. 

- Investigate a performance or production issue. 

- Work with product and frontend to shape a new feature. 

- Review code and help teammates improve. 

- Build backend tools that our AI agents use to perform real finance operations. 

- Design safe, deterministic workflows where agents propose actions and humans review them. 

Your time will be split between building new features and improving what already exists . Both matter. 

You won’t just build endpoints. You’ll help shape the execution layer that our agents rely on: the APIs, data models, and workflows that let them act safely in production. 

You’ll work closely with product, frontend, and customer-facing teams. We expect engineers to take ownership of parts of the system and help make them more reliable over time. 

💻 Our current tech reality 

Our stack evolves based on our challenges, but we care more about good design than trendy tools 🙏 

Python is our core language. It helps us move fast, keep the code readable, and fits naturally with our AI-driven approach. A growing part of the system is built around agents that use our backend as a set of reliable, deterministic tools. 

- Core language: Python 

- Backend: FastAPI + Pydantic 

- Data: PostgreSQL 

- Infra: AWS, serverless when it makes sense 

- Performance: some Rust for critical paths 

- Architecture: multi-service backend, simple enough to reason about 

Some parts of the system are clean and well-tested. Others were built quickly and need love. That’s the phase we’re in. 

Over the next year, we’ll focus on: 

- Turning core workflows into reliable tools for our agents 

- Simplifying services 

- Improving tests and observability 

- Making performance more predictable 

- Cleaning up early code 

We know we’re not perfect, but we care a lot about improving step by step. 

✨ Who’s going to thrive with us 

You’ll probably feel comfortable here if: 

- You like building products people actually use. 

- You are autonomous and take ownership of what you ship. 

- You take initiative and lead by example. 

- You’re curious and enjoy figuring things out. 

- You’re pragmatic about trade-offs. 

- You communicate with kindness and clarity. 

This role is a great fit if you’re excited by the idea of: 

- Building systems that are used by AI agents, not just humans. 

- Designing reliable, safe automation in production. 

- Working on a product that is still early and evolving quickly. 

You don’t need to know everything about AI. But you should be curious about it and excited to work in a system where agents are part of the core product 🤖 

🧩 What you’ll get from this role 

- Real ownership over parts of the system. 

- Direct impact on customers and product decisions. 

- A small, human team where your work is visible and meaningful 🤝 

- A mix of feature work, system design, and technical improvements. 

- Exposure to real scaling and production challenges. 

- The chance to help build an agent-driven product from the inside. 

We offer: 

- Competitive salary and equity. 

- Flexible remote setup (we prefer people to come into Paris or London office twice per week. At a minimum we’d ask you to be at an office 3 days per month, onboard in Paris for your first few weeks, and work CEST timezone). 

- A high-autonomy environment where you have real ownership and space to make an impact. 

- Plenty of room to grow, take responsibility, and shape parts of the product. 

- A culture based on trust, ownership, and clear communication. 

This isn’t a huge corporate environment. In exchange, you get autonomy, responsibility, and the chance to shape a product that’s still early in its story—and help build what finance operations will look like in the next decade 🚀

title: Customer Success Leader, Southern Europe & DACH
description:
Why Harvey 

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview 

As the Enterprise Customer Success Leader, you are tasked with more than just facilitating the adoption of our technology. As a member of the broader Customer Success Leadership team, you will craft and execute a strategic vision for ensuring customers reach their desired outcomes, emphasizing scalability, process rigor, and the development of playbooks to fuel expansion and mitigate churn.

Through empathetic leadership and a focus on value, you will spearhead efforts to enhance renewal and expansion rates, manage and develop talent, and drive forward customer relationships with proactive engagement.

You will also play an integral part in helping to drive strategy and execution in how we deliver an end-to-end excellent customer experience.

What You'll Do 

- Lead by Example: Lead a dynamic customer success team towards exceptional performance, promoting a culture of accountability, execution, growth, and relentless improvement.

- Scalability and Process: Develop and implement strategic improvements to drive scalable strategies and playbooks, ensuring a systematic approach to all stages of the customer journey, including: implementation, adoption, value realization, retention, and expansion.

- Talent Coaching and Development: Inspire and mentor your team, elevating their capabilities to become strategic partners through influencing and advising decision makers and fostering customer advocacy.

- Advance Customer Relationships: Deepen client engagements through strategic interactions, serving as an advisor and advocate for key stakeholders, driving advocacy, organic growth, and referrals.

- Own Retention: introduce processes and early warning systems to reduce churn, mitigate risk, and ensure we are multi-threaded within customer accounts.

- Effective Collaboration: Work with leaders across the broader GTM organization, Product, and Engineering teams to deliver the voice-of-customer and drive a culture of customer-centricity.

- Product Feedback: Ensure we develop a feedback flywheel, turning customer insights into meaningful product enhancements and service optimizations.

What You Have 

- Leadership Experience: You are a natural leader, with a proven background in leading high performing customer success teams within late-stage or post-IPO Enterprise SaaS organizations, with a specific emphasis on “Strategic”, “Large Enterprise / Enterprise”, and/or top-tier / lighthouse accounts with multi-million dollar spend.

- Strategic Acumen: Expertise in designing and executing customer success strategies that foster adoption, reduce churn, and promote expansion.

- Empathy and Influence: A leadership style characterized by empathy, with a proven track record in team development through hiring, coaching, and fostering talent.

- Outcome-Oriented: Exceptional ability to drive results through owning strategic initiatives, KPI reporting, and adept at navigating complex customer scenarios.

- Communication Mastery: Superior communication skills, capable of effectively engaging and influencing at all organizational levels both internally, and externally.

- Agility: Capacity to excel in a rapidly expanding, dynamic setting and swiftly adjust to evolving requirements.

- Innovation: A genuine passion for technology and innovation, constantly seeking novel solutions to complex challenges.

title: Senior Applied Scientist - Behavior AI
description:
The Behavior AI team builds the AI-based anomaly detection behind Datadog's security products. Our models learn what normal looks like across the billions of logs, events, and telemetry records flowing through the platform every second, and they flag the behavior that does not fit, on every record, in real time, at a cost that makes sense at our scale. What we build does not ship to a single feature. The same models power detection across many of Datadog's security products at once, so the work has impact well beyond any one team. Large general-purpose models are too slow and too expensive to run in that path, so we take the opposite approach: small, custom models, designed for high-throughput stream processing and optimized to run cheaply on every record.

We are hiring a Senior Applied Scientist to build these models from start to finish. You will contribute to designing the architecture, training at scale, and the optimization work that takes a model from training to running efficiently on production traffic. This optimization requires a deep understanding of the constraints imposed by both the software and the hardware, together with the applied mathematics to work within them: often it comes down to finding a mathematical reformulation that fits those constraints better, and that judgment can decide whether a model reaches production at all.

The work involves a number of open questions. How do you obtain most of the quality of a large model from one that is far smaller and cheap enough to run on the full stream? Where is it worth trading exactness for speed, and how do you reason about the error you accept? How do you make a small model's outputs clear enough that the detection engineers and analysts who rely on it can trust what it reports? If these are the problems you want to work on, we would like to hear from you.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture: the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. 

What You'll Do: 

- Design and build custom mid-size models for high-throughput stream processing, and train them at scale.

- Optimize these models from start to finish, working across both the mathematics and the systems, often by finding mathematical reformulations that fit the hardware and software constraints better.

- Build the training data pipelines the work depends on when they do not already exist, from the raw stream to a training-ready dataset.

- Work with engineering to integrate models into production, with a clear focus on GPU utilization, latency, and cost per record on live traffic.

- Plan the roadmap of model and system improvements, based on a solid understanding of the product and of what matters most to users.

- Build an agentic layer on top of the models to analyze, validate, and act on their outputs.

- Build lightweight interpretability tools that make model behavior easier to explain to the people who rely on it.

- Maintain and monitor the models, services, and infrastructure your team owns, and take part in your team's on-call rotation.

Who You Are: 

- You have a BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, or a related scientific field, or equivalent experience.

- You have hands-on experience training and fine-tuning models at scale, and deploying them into production systems with real throughput and cost constraints.

- You have a working knowledge of how GPUs work, and a track record of making models run efficiently within real hardware constraints.

- You have strong applied-mathematics fundamentals and reach for them naturally when designing and optimizing models.

- You have a real passion for applied mathematics, software design, and implementation. This role sits at the intersection of the three, and it is a requirement for the position.

- You care about code simplicity and performance, and you can build the data pipelines and the surrounding production code, in addition to the models themselves.

- You can explain complex ideas and trade-offs clearly to engineers and product partners, and you let a solid understanding of the product guide what you build next.

- Bonus: experience with efficient sequence architectures, model interpretability, or large-scale streaming systems.

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you're passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

title: Product Line Manager
description:
About Wallee Group AG

Wallee Group is a leader in advanced payment solutions, dedicated to providing robust, scalable, and secure systems across multiple domains. We enhance customer experiences through innovative payment and finance technology that empowers businesses to grow efficiently. With operations spanning several countries, we thrive on collaboration and agility, utilizing the Scrum framework to drive our international teams. At Wallee, we stay at the forefront of market trends, continuously innovating to deliver premier services to our global customers.

The Role 

The Product Line Manager owns the full lifecycle of a product line - from introduction through to controlled end-of-life. The role combines strategic portfolio and roadmap management with subject matter expertise in specific verticals, bringing market, product, and supplier perspectives into one consistent strategy.

In Wallee's payment technology context, this specifically includes managing hardware/firmware generations (e.g., terminal models, certification versions like the EMV L2 kernel) and forward-looking planning for successor products.

The Impact You’ll Make 

- Drive Full Lifecycle & Strategy: Own the product journey from concept to decommissioning—defining launch criteria, target segments, success metrics, and forward-looking successor products before hardware/firmware generation changes.

- Optimize the Portfolio: Maintain a structured view of all variants (terminal types, SoftPOS vs. hardware POS) using frameworks like the BCG matrix to prioritize investment and avoid overlap/cannibalization.

- Build Capacity-Synced Roadmaps: Translate strategic goals and vertical needs into prioritized, time-boxed feature roadmaps (e.g., quarterly or PI planning in SAFe), balancing "run the business" compliance updates against "grow the business" initiatives.

- Champion Vertical Expertise & Research: Act as the "translator" between vertical requirements (e.g., retail, hospitality, events) and engineering's technical language while running ongoing trend scanning (PCI/EMV updates), competitor analysis, and customer feedback synthesis.

- Lead Go-to-Market & Sales Enablement: Define launch plans (positioning, pricing, training, documentation), coordinate alignment across Sales, Marketing, and Support, and assist Sales with technical expertise on complex, regulated deals.

- Manage Suppliers & Ecosystems: Onboard and manage external partners (terminal manufacturers, component suppliers, certification labs), overseeing SLAs, operational forecasting, defect escalations, contract negotiations, and risk mitigation (such as dual-sourcing).

What Success Looks Like 

- Strategic Portfolio Health: A clear, non-overlapping product line where investments are prioritized effectively and End-of-Sale (EOS) / End-of-Life (EOL) migration paths are seamlessly executed.

- Uncompromising Compliance: Continuous alignment with certification and regulatory standards (PCI, EMV, ep2) across the entire portfolio, eliminating compliance risk.

- Reliable Supplier Alignment: High-performing partner relationships with well-managed SLAs, aligned roadmaps, and secure supply chains.

- Market-Driven Innovation: Roadmaps and GTM materials that accurately reflect vertical user journeys, market trends, and validated customer needs.

- Cross-Functional Readiness: Seamless coordination with internal teams so all departments are aligned and fully enabled from day one of product launches.

What You Bring to the Table 

- Product Experience: Proven experience in product management, ideally with portfolio or product line ownership in fintech, payments, or hardware-enabled software.

- Domain Knowledge: Understanding or familiarity with payment certification and compliance topics (PCI, EMV, ep2) is a strong plus.

- Vertical & Market Expertise: Experience or strong interest in specific industry verticals, coupled with a track record in market research and competitor analysis.

- Strategic & Analytical Mindset: Strong problem-solving skills with a solution- and customer-oriented approach.

- Stakeholder & Supplier Management: Exceptional communication and negotiation skills, comfortable managing both internal stakeholders and external supplier relationships.

- Languages: Fluent in English and German.

Why Join Wallee? 

- Modern Workspace: A beautiful office in the heart of Winterthur - comfortable, bright, and collaboration-ready.

- True Flexibility: Flexible daily hours and a 4-week "Work from Anywhere" policy every year.

- Innovation First: We work with the latest tech stacks in a flat hierarchy where your voice actually matters.

- Growth & Culture: Competitive compensation , aligned with experience, seniority, and expertise, personal development budgets , and a social calendar filled with events .

- The Perks: Fresh fruits, snacks, and high-quality coffee to keep you fueled.

Don’t tick every box? Neither do most great hires. If the role feels right, reach out, we’d love to see if we’re a match.

title: Mechanisch monteur
Senior MLOps Engineer, Buyer
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

The Buyer domain's Data Science teams build and iterate on our most critical ML systems—like ranking, retrieval, and recommendations—that serve millions of users. As our ambition and the complexity of these models grow, we are scaling our MLOps capabilities to match: 

We are hiring an MLOps Engineer to solve this. This is a high-impact "bridge" role, not to build new platforms, but to be the expert user of our existing platforms (GCP/Vertex AI, Vespa, Triton). Your mission is to take our Data Science team's work, rectify the current ad-hoc solutions, and build the robust, automated, and high-quality "path-to-production" our advanced models require.

Also by joining Vinted, you’ll become part of an active community of engineers who are keen on sharing knowledge, organizing learning workshops and so much more!

In this position, you’ll 

- Productionise ML models: be responsible for migrating all existing model training code from experimental or proof-of-concept stages to robust and automated pipelines.

- Build continuous training (CT) pipelines: design, build, and maintain automated workflows for data preparation, model training, and batch scoring.

- Automate model serving & integration: package and deploy traditional ML models (e.g., in ONNX format) to our existing serving infrastructure, primarily Vespa and/or Triton.

- Close the deployment loop: automate model deployments where they are still manual. For example, building a GitHub Action that deploys a new model to Vespa, triggered by a webhook from a successful Vertex AI training pipeline.

- Build the missing quality gates: build the automated quality and evaluation gates that our pipelines lack today. This includes:

- Establish and uphold ML Model Lifecycle Standards: Take ownership of and continuously improve the standards, quality, and governance of the complete ML model lifecycle.

About you 

- We are looking for an "ML-literate" Software Engineer, not a Data Scientist. You are a builder and an automator with a strong service mindset.

- Must-have technical skills: deep expertise in GCP/Vertex AI (or equivalents like SageMaker), Kubernetes, and Docker.

- Automation expertise: proven experience building robust CI/CD and automation pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.).

- ML-Literate: you understand ML workflows and concepts (training, evaluation, inference) well enough to debug pipelines and build meaningful quality gates.

- Soft skills: a strong "service mindset," excellent communication, and the ability to act as a bridge between the highly technical worlds of Data Science and Infrastructure. You are pragmatic and driven to get high-quality work into production.

- Bonus Points: familiarity with ML serving platforms like Vespa search engine or NVIDIA Triton and model formats like ONNX.

- Willingness to learn and master new technologies and concepts.

- We value pragmatism, big-picture thinking, curiosity, and problem-solving skills.

title: Full Stack Developer (Onboarding & Enablement)
description:
We turn every customer interaction into an opportunity. We connect conversations, customer data and payments with AI Agents so that companies can deliver personal customer journeys at scale: both online and in person.

“The entire customer journey. One platform”

What we value 

Every CM.com colleague, connects to our 4 shared values :

Drive and Lead 

You take initiative, make decisions and recognize opportunities. Making mistakes is part of moving forward.

Grow and Learn 

The growth of our colleagues and our customers is our priority. You like to experiment, learn continuously and actively share knowledge and insights with others.

Together and Care 

We work together and we believe that diverse perspectives lead to stronger outcomes. You value the social side of work, you show genuine interest and care about one another’s well-being.

Speed and Change 

By welcoming AI Agents into our organisation, we fundamentally change how work is done. You are comfortable with change and you love working in a high paced environment.

The Role 

As a Full Stack Developer in the Onboarding & Enablement team, you'll own the front door of CM.com connectivity: the self service experience where customers sign up and start messaging in minutes, without a sales call or a single email. It is one of the most important topics at CM.com today, and your team is the conductor behind it.

In today's tech market, speed wins. Customers choose the provider they can start with right now, and they value ease over a long list of requirements. Think of how quickly you can take out a phone subscription: that is the experience we want to offer. Our customers are people, but increasingly also AI agents, and neither wants to wait for a callback.

Behind that one simple interface sits a complex platform. Every channel works differently. For example: WhatsApp runs via Meta, RCS via Google and Orange, and more channels and suppliers are joining. Customers should never notice any of that. The complexity is ours, not theirs.

You will 

- Build the self service onboarding experience that takes customers from sign up to their first message in minutes

- Turn every customer request into the right configuration across our own systems and external suppliers, fully automated

- Make it easy to plug in new channels and supplier partnerships, so the platform grows without adding complexity for the customer

- Drive automation across the full customer journey, for people and AI agents alike

- Own your work from idea to production, including how it runs on our infrastructure

- Use AI tools actively to improve your own work: experiment, automate, and share what works with your team

- Medior to senior full stack developer with hands on experience in both front end and back end

- Strong in Angular on the front end, and in C# and .NET on the back end

- Solid knowledge of relational databases, such as SQL Server or PostgreSQL

- Fluent in English and Dutch

- Nice to have: experience with DevOps or system engineering, as the team also manages its own infrastructure

- Genuinely curious about AI: you experiment with tools like ChatGPT or Copilot and you're open to working differently as they improve

Believe you’d be a great fit for this role, even if you don’t tick every box? Reach out to our Recruitment team! We’d be happy to connect and see if we can make it work together.

What we offer 

As a CM.com club member, you’ll have the following benefits:

- Onboarding : Join our unique 3-days Global Onboarding program in our Headquarters in Breda, a deep dive into the culture of CM.com.

- Healthy food: Daily healthy lunches and snacks to keep you energized.

- Effortless commute: The Shuttle mobility card, commuting allowance and Lease-a-bike options get you where you need to be. We have CM company cars that you can use for client visits as well.

- Invest in your future : A solid pension plan.

- Time off: Recharge with 25 vacation days, plus the option to purchase 10 additional days.

- Own your success: Become a shareholder with our Employee Share Purchase Program.

- Your Development : We support your growth and development through initiatives like the CM Academy, Udemy courses, exclusive meetups with thought leaders, the Young Professional Program, and our own CM Business Adventure (CMBA), ensuring you’re always learning and evolving

- Vitality : Our Vitality Team organizes a year-round vitality program to support a healthy body and mind for all colleagues. Think of stress prevention workshops, ergonomist visit, weekly bootcamps, yoga sessions and our CM sports day.

- Together at CM.com : Weekly drinks, board game nights, karaoke throwdowns, yearly ski trip, and more! We have something for everyone.

Our diverse perspectives fuel innovation and drive us forward. We welcome everyone, regardless of age, background, or beliefs.

Before you apply 

We work on-site, move fast, and expect you to bring your own thinking. Priorities shift, AI is actively changing how we work and we embrace that reality. If that sounds like a great environment to you, we'd love to hear from you.

Note: For this position, we can only consider candidates who already hold a permanent work and residence permit for the Netherlands.

title: Web & Mobile Full Stack Developer
description:
The mission 
Help build fair, engaged and high-performing teams.
We believe everyone deserves a fair opportunity to develop and be rewarded for the value they bring. That’s why we build software that helps organizations set clear expectations, define what a role entails, assess performance fairly, support employee growth, and make compensation transparent and explainable. From clear roles to fair rewards, all within one continuous process. Will you join us in driving this change?

Please note: for this role, it’s important that you already live in the Netherlands and are able to work from our Utrecht office at least three days a week.

The opportunity 
As our new Web & Mobile Full Stack Developer, you’ll help build and improve our SaaS platform across all surfaces: mobile, web and backend. You’ll work on our React Native mobile app as we scale it into a fully independent experience for mobile-first markets. You’ll contribute just as actively to our web platform, from intuitive user interfaces in React to scalable APIs and backend services in Node.js .

Your average week in Utrecht:

- Building and shipping new features in our React Native mobile app (around 50% of your time)

- Building and shipping new features on our web platform, with React on the frontend and Node.js on the backend (around 50% of your time)

- Shaping features together with product and design to improve the user experience

- Working in structured weekly sprints with your team

- Writing clean, scalable and maintainable code in TypeScript, React, React Native, Node.js and MongoDB

- Building and improving performant, secure REST APIs

- Contributing to technical discussions and architecture decisions, including our mobile strategy

- Reviewing pull requests to keep quality high

- Improving developer workflows, CI/CD and automated testing

- Owning features from idea to deployment, across mobile and web

In short: your work directly makes our platform faster, smarter and more scalable, helping our customers grow and pushing Learned to the next level 🌱

The team 
You’ll join a development team of 6 developers in Utrecht, working closely with 11 colleagues in Sri Lanka through a buddy system that keeps lines short. The team is led by Alex, our CTO. We’re an international company of 55 people (7+ nationalities) serving 350+ customers, increasingly at enterprise level. With the EU Pay Transparency Directive coming up, demand for our product is growing fast, and so is our roadmap.

Your growth 

- Learning every day from experienced, senior colleagues across mobile, web and backend

- Hands-on experience building AI features into a product used by hundreds of companies

- A personal development budget of €1,000 per year

- An open feedback culture: we practice what we preach

The musts 

- You already live in the Netherlands and can work from our Utrecht office at least 3 days a week

- Around 3+ years of experience as a Full Stack Developer

- At least 1 year of experience building production apps in React Native

- Solid experience with TypeScript, React and Node.js (or comparable stacks), including REST APIs

- Experience building or integrating AI features in a product (e.g. LLM features, agents or retrieval)

- You enjoy switching between mobile, frontend and backend, and owning features end-to-end

- You communicate clearly and confidently in English

- You’re proactive, take ownership and love learning together through feedback

The nice-to-haves 

- Experience with MongoDB or similar databases

- Experience with CI/CD, automated testing and cloud infrastructure

- Experience publishing apps to the App Store and Google Play

- Experience in B2B SaaS, ideally HR tech

The benefits 

- A salary between €4,000 and €5,500 gross per month (based on 40 hours, depending on experience), with room to grow

- 25 vacation days (based on full-time)

- A pension plan (10%, of which we pay 50%)

- A personal development budget of €1,000 per year (based on full-time)

- A MacBook Pro and everything you need to do your job well

- Travel expense reimbursement via our mobility plan

- A hybrid setup: at least 3 days at the office, flexible beyond that

- The option to work remotely from abroad for up to 6 weeks per year

- Daily healthy lunches, Friday drinks and monthly team activities 🎉

- An ambitious, international environment where we challenge each other and celebrate wins together

Sounds good? 🙌 We’d love to hear from you. Who knows, we might be meeting each other soon.

title: Junior Product Manager – IT Fulfillment
description:

As Junior Product Manager for IT Fulfillment, you will help build and improve the services that make that happen: the order flows, data and interfaces that connect our webstore, our stores, our warehouses and our customer service teams.

You will work in a small team inside the IT Fulfillment domain, alongside the Group Product Manager and our own engineers. The Group Product Manager shapes the functional direction with the business and sets priorities; together you turn it into clear requirements, well-defined tickets and working software, built with engineers and AI agents. This is a technical product role: we build our own services, so you will spend your time in data models, interfaces and requirements rather than managing a vendor’s roadmap. You start close to delivery, with support while you learn the domain, and grow into owning more of the roadmap.

What you will do 

- Turn mapped-out functional flows into clear, buildable work: technical requirements, acceptance criteria and user stories that engineers and AI agents can pick up without coming back with questions.

- Own the detail as both product manager and business analyst: the data model, the way systems talk to each other, and the edge cases nobody thought of yet.

- Break large changes into chunks that can be built, tested and released safely, and keep the backlog in a state where work can start at any moment.

- Work with engineers day to day in refinement, planning, reviews and releases, and use our AI tooling to draft, structure and pressure-test the work before it reaches them.

- Design our order data and interfaces so that AI agents can read, reason over and act on them as reliably as our own systems do.

- Create visibility across the end-to-end fulfillment journey, so anyone from a customer service agent to a supply chain lead can see where an order is and what happened to it, and turn that into measures the business trusts.

- Take on discovery for smaller and mid-sized roadmap items as your domain knowledge builds: the options, the trade-offs and the recommendation.

Who you are 

- Business analysis experience: 2+ years of hands-on experience as a Business Analyst or Product Owner. You have written functional and technical specifications, worked directly with developers, and been accountable for the detail being right. The analysis craft is what we are hiring for.

- Domain experience: That experience is in fulfillment, order management, supply chain, e-commerce or retail operations. You know what an order, a shipment, an allocation and a return actually are, and what it costs operationally when one goes wrong.

- Eye for detail: You chase the last open question rather than leaving it for someone else to find in production.

- AI-native mindset: You already work with tools like Claude and Cursor every day to analyse, draft, prototype and check your own thinking, and you know what to hand over and what to validate yourself.

- Technical fluency: You can hold your own in a technical conversation without being an engineer, and you say “I don’t understand that yet” rather than guessing.

- Communication: You are a clear writer who asks the uncomfortable question early rather than the polite one late.

- Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Technology, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

What you will get 

- Autonomy: We empower you to take ownership, make meaningful decisions, and drive impact close to our customers.

- Growth: You will develop within a high-performance digital product environment, increasing your business impact and decision scope over time.

- Corporate Social Responsibility: Our commitment to sustainability and ethical business is unwavering. We work exclusively with suppliers who uphold the highest standards, in alignment with the International Labour Organization.

- Style: Immerse yourself in a world of beautifully crafted, high-quality products, and enjoy a 40% discount on Suitsupply products.

- Compensation: We offer a competitive salary based on relevant skills and experience.

title: Events & Community Manager
description:
About us: 

Tebi is creating the first Connected Restaurant Management System that makes hospitality flow. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen prep, payments, and all the data that powers it, creating smooth service and intuitive insights.

About the role: 

Restaurant owners trust other restaurant owners. They listen to the chef down the street, their wine supplier and their accountant long before they listen to an ad. That's why our events work. When we launched in Berlin, we hosted a four-hands dinner with two local merchants and a well-known food creator. You’ll plan and run our partner and owned events, and find new ways to grow Tebi through the hospitality community in each city, neighbourhood and market. You’ll work closely with our local sales teams so every event and partnership turns into real conversations.

This is a hands-on role. One week you'll be hosting a merchant dinner in Milan, the next you'll be setting up a distributor breakfast in Amsterdam. You'll report to the Head of Marketing and work closely with our Marketing team to extend these programs to our channel ecosystem, plus align closely with the General Managers and Account Managers in each market.

What you'll be doing: 

- Run events across markets: Plan and deliver partner and owned events in 2–3 markets at a time, from intimate merchant dinners and industry breakfasts to city launches. You own the calendar, budget, venues, suppliers, guest lists and the plan for the night.

- Build the playbook as you go: Turn each event into templates, checklists and supplier lists, so we can launch a city campaign in weeks, not months. Improve them after every event.

- Build local partner networks: Find the people operators already trust: drinks distributors, wholesalers, food creators, hospitality associations, accountants and the advisers who help new venues open. Build partnerships that bring us introductions and referrals, not just logos.

- Put our merchants front and center: Work with our best merchants as hosts and anchors, so prospects hear about Tebi from the people they respect.

- Turn connections into pipeline: Agree with local Sales and Account Management who to involve, how to follow up and who owns what conversations. Track every event in HubSpot from invite to demo to signed merchant.

- Grow Tebi through the community: Find new ways to reach operators through the people and places they already trust, in each city, neighborhood and across borders. Keep guests and partners engaged after events, so one introduction leads to the next.

- Open new community channels: Test new ways to grow through our close-knit industry, such as an affiliate or referral program for partners, sharing useful insights from our merchants, and showing up in the forums and groups where operators talk shop.

- Capture the stories: Work with our creative team and relevant freelancers to turn events and partner moments into social content, case studies and sales material.

How we'll measure success: 

- Events delivered each quarter across markets, on time and on budget

- Demos, pipeline and new merchants from each event and partnership

- Introductions, referrals and leads from partners, affiliates and community channels

- Cost per demo compared with our other channels

What you’ll bring: 

- Have built something people show up for: an event series, a supper club, a community, a program. You can point to what it led to, not just how many people came

- Feel at home in hospitality. You've worked in or around restaurants, bars or food and drink brands, and you're comfortable leading a room full of operators

- Are high agency. You own your calendar, your relationships and your results, and you don't wait to be told what to do

- Build your own playbook when there isn't one, and you enjoy doing the work as much as planning it

- Know the difference between a real community and a guest list

- See growth opportunities beyond events, and are curious enough to test them

- Can run several markets at once without dropping details, and are happy to travel regularly

- Track what you do: comfortable with a CRM (HubSpot a plus), UTMs and simple reporting

- Speak fluent English. Dutch, German, Italian, Spanish or a Nordic language is a plus

This role isn't for you if: 

- You'd rather plan the program than run it

- You need a fixed playbook and a clear org chart to get going

- You're not willing to roll up your sleeves on the night

Benefits: 

- Start-up Equity

- Competitive Salary

- Lunch Provided in Office

- Team building events

- Unlimited time off

What is Restaurant Software? 

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How we use AI at Tebi

We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn’t make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

title: Senior Specialist, T2 / Target2 Payment Operations
description:
About Finom 

Finom is a European tech startup headquartered in Amsterdam, and we’re on a journey towards revolutionizing the financial landscape for entrepreneurs worldwide. Our mission is to develop an all-in-one financial B2B solution that integrates banking functions, accounting, financial management, and invoicing into a seamless, mobile-first platform.

We recently closed a €115 million Series C equity round (around $133 million), bringing our total funding to approximately $346 million. Finom's platform goes beyond traditional banking, offering invoicing and a growing suite of features, including AI-enabled accounting, aiming to simplify financial management for entrepreneurs. At Finom, we’re not just redefining the entrepreneurial experience — we’re empowering our employees to make a real difference. Your work matters, and your impact extends far beyond product metrics. We nurture innovation and an inspiring work environment where bold ideas thrive, prioritizing thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and our business as a whole.

Maintaining our start-up spirit, we prioritize thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and, of course, our business.

Senior Specialist, T2 (Target2) Payment Operations 

Location: Remote in Netherlands, Spain, Cyprus or Poland

The role

We’re moving from indirect to direct participation in TARGET2 (T2), and we need someone to own the operational side end to end. You’ll design and document the Payment Operations processes, validate them in the August UAT, cut over BIC by BIC, and then run them as business-as-usual. You’ll be the operational contact for the T2 scheme, DNB and our partner banks.

What you’ll do

- Own core payment processes: SCT / SCT Inst recalls, investigations (including pacs.028), SWIFT enquiries (MT199/MT999, RFIs), missing or incoming funds, and rejects, returns and refunds.

- Run the T2 platform day to day: work in the T2 GUI (U2A/A2A), maintain CRDM reference data, and set up four-eyes controls and the manual-vs-automated split.

- Manage the migration: move traffic from BNP Paribas to direct participation, with every payment traceable by BIC and path, and define when each BNPP-dependent step can be retired.

- Cover reconciliation and liquidity: be the Payment Ops link to the reconciliation team (funding and defunding stay with Finance Ops/Treasury).

- Handle incidents and contingency: build the incident process around DNB, FIS and TARGET escalation routes, own Payment Ops’ role in DNB reporting, and define the ECONS II contingency approach.

- Coordinate with others: work with the Eurosystem, DNB, SWIFT/NEXI, FIS and correspondent banks, and partner with Product and Engineering to specify how the platform should behave.

What success looks like

- Every direct-participation process has an owner, documented procedures, and passing UAT evidence.

- The migration causes no impact on customers, and Customer Support has clear guidance.

- After go-live, T2 runs as stable BAU with no remaining BNPP operational dependency.

What we’re looking for

- Hands-on experience with T2 / TARGET Services (RTGS, TIPS), including the GUI and U2A/A2A actions

- Around 2-3+ years in payment operations at a bank, EMI or PSP, ideally with SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst)

- Familiarity with investigations, recalls, returns and SWIFT / ISO 20022 messaging

- Experience writing SOPs and controls, or the ability to pick it up quickly

- Comfort working with regulators, partners and technical teams

- Enough ownership to make sign-off and escalation decisions with support from the team

- Fluent English

Nice to have

- Experience with CRDM reference-data maintenance

- Involvement in a direct-participation onboarding or sponsor-bank migration

- Knowledge of DNB / TARGET-NL conditions, IPR, PSD2, or ECONS II contingency processes
