This is a high-impact, quota-carrying role ideal for a self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, data-driven environment and is passionate about helping performance marketers scale through programmatic app advertising.

You'll join a high-performing team spanning EMEA Sales, Client Growth, and Media Buying under App Performance Solutions — a team that will actively support your growth and success within the InMobi programmatic sales ecosystem. This is an exciting opportunity to make a visible impact across the EMEA region for a high-growth App Performance Solutions business comprising an AI/ML-driven DSP, Owned and Operated Glance TV, and Performance CTV.

This is a role for true hunters — those who thrive on building pipelines from scratch, opening doors others can't, and turning cold conversations into long-term revenue partnerships.

This is a fully remote role based in Germany. Proficiency in both German and English is required. Some travel is expected for client meetings, industry events, and in-person team sync-ups as needed. 

The Impact You'll Make: 

As Senior Sales Manager, EMEA, you will be responsible for driving sales from a portfolio of Direct Brands and Performance Agencies across the DACH region by creating and selling effective App Performance Solutions. You will also actively participate in shaping InMobi's App Performance sales strategy, go-to-market approach, and execution plan across your key region within EMEA.

- Identify, acquire, advise, and develop new relationships with targeted, strategic brands, agencies, and partners that ensure the growth and long-term success of InMobi's suite of App Performance Solutions

- Leverage your knowledge of the market landscape and InMobi's unique selling propositions and differentiators to develop new and enduring business with advertisers — including navigating the Programmatic and walled garden ecosystems to position InMobi App Performance Solutions as a must-have for brands' app growth and retention strategies

- Maintain strong relationships with ecosystem influencers, MMPs, agencies, and partners to keep InMobi top of mind for their clients

- Own the entire sales lifecycle — from outbound prospecting and inbound lead qualification to proposal building, nurturing, activation, and strategic growth consulting

- Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams across Client Growth, Media Buying, Legal, Finance, Ecosystem Partnerships, and Product to ensure seamless onboarding, execution, and account handover to the Growth team

- Represent InMobi App Performance Solutions at key industry events, conferences, and networking opportunities across EMEA to drive visibility and pipeline growth

- Maintain a disciplined approach to pipeline management, leveraging CRM tools for accurate forecasting and performance tracking

- Consistently exceed quarterly revenue targets through strategic account acquisition and strong client relationship management

- Industry experience . You bring 5+ years of hunting and selling experience to App businesses and Performance Agencies. - An advertising technology expert . You've spent at least 6+ years in ad tech and know the EMEA ecosystem well. In a marketplace flooded with vendors, your clients think of you first — not because you sold them, but because you solved for them.

- Analytically strong and a compelling storyteller . You have strong analytical skills and the ability to peel back layers and find hidden opportunities. You don't just present numbers — you build narratives around them that move clients to action.

- A proactive problem solver . You have a proven ability to solve customer pain points and technical challenges while proactively creating solutions through cross-functional collaboration.

- Eager, curious, and a fast learner . You are naturally inquisitive, take a proactive approach, and seek out ways to support your colleagues. The ad tech landscape shifts constantly — signal loss, AI disruption, shifting buyer behaviour — and you lean in rather than wait for the dust to settle.

- Education . A BA/BS degree in a relevant discipline is required, or equivalent professional experience. An MBA or Master's degree is a plus.

- Language . Full professional proficiency in both German and English is required.

- Believe in lifelong learning — we welcome feedback, challenge ourselves to grow, and aren't afraid to take smart risks

Our compensation philosophy enables us to provide a competitive salary that drives high performance while balancing business needs and pay equity. We determine compensation based on a wide variety of factors, including role, nature of experience, skills, and location.

The base salary or fixed pay for this role ranges from €132,500 to €167,250 (min to max of base salary). title: Head of Product
description:
Head of Product (m/f/d) | Berlin | Full-Time 

Location: Berlin, Germany (office first)
Start date: As soon as possible
Company: Venture-backed AI startup, early stage

About the Company 

We’re a fast-growing AI company building agents for complex, high-stakes enterprise workflows in public procurement, one of Europe’s largest and least digitised markets. Our product takes on the slow, manual, document-heavy work behind public tenders. That saves businesses and the public sector a great deal of wasted time and money.

The Role 

We’re hiring a Head of Product to own and scale our product function. This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You’ll be the most senior product person in the company and work directly with the founders and engineering team. You’ll personally drive discovery, prioritisation and delivery. As we grow, you’ll set up how the product function works: its processes, rituals and culture. When the time is right, you’ll hire the team around you.

What You’ll Do 

- Own the product strategy and roadmap, setting direction alongside the founders, engineering and customers.
- Lead core product initiatives end to end, from discovery and scoping through launch and iteration. You’ll ship AI products that enterprise customers rely on.
- Stay close to the product: test, refine and pressure-test our agents, and understand how prompts, context and evaluations shape quality.
- Spend real time with customers. Uncover requirements, turn noisy feedback into clear priorities and become a trusted partner to their business.
- Build the product function. Define how we discover, prioritise, ship and measure, and lay the foundations for a future product team.
- Work with GTM on positioning and join sales conversations where product insight wins deals.

Who You Are 

- 5+ years in product management or a closely related role (founder, early operator, consulting into product), with a strong record of shipping.
- A startup operator at heart. You’ve done your best work at early-stage companies, ideally as one of the first product hires or as a founder. Experience only at large corporates won’t be the right fit for this role.
- A strong all-rounder, as comfortable setting strategy as writing a detailed spec, debugging an edge case or jumping on a sales call.
- Exceptional product sense and user empathy. You look past the surface of a feature request to find the root problem.
- Technically curious. You don’t need a CS degree or coding skills, but you’re confident working with engineers and exploring what AI can and can’t do.
- A clear communicator who uses both qualitative and quantitative reasoning to make and explain decisions.
- Based in Berlin or ready to relocate.
- Fluent in English and German (required for our customer base).
- Nice to have: B2B or enterprise software experience (strongly preferred), hands-on work with AI/LLM products, or exposure to public sector or regulated markets.

You’ll Thrive If 

- You love building from 0 to 1. You don’t need a roadmap handed to you, and you enjoy creating structure where there is none.
- You move fast and are energised by an intense, ambitious environment.
- You have a “no task is too small” mindset and lead by doing.
- You love being in the office and believe in-person collaboration drives speed.

What’s In It For You 

- Ownership from day one. You’ll define the product, with direct access to the founders and zero red tape.
- A role that grows with you. As the company scales, so do your scope and your team.
- Shared upside: top-of-market compensation and generous equity.
- A mission that matters. You won’t be optimising ad clicks. You’ll be helping businesses and the public sector cut waste on a huge scale.

Our Process 

- Review: All applications reviewed within 5 days.
- Intro call: 30 minutes on your background and motivations.
- Product deep dive (remote): 1 hour on your product thinking and problem-solving.
- On-site (half day): Work through a real product use case with the team, followed by 1:1s with Engineering and GTM.
- Offer: A quick final decision and transparent feedback straight after the on-site.

How to Apply 

Apply through this posting with:

- Your CV
- A few lines on what excites you about this role
- Optional: links to products you’ve shipped

We're looking for a Staff Data Scientist, Pricing to build the analytical and machine learning capability that pricing runs on, from demand modelling through to the systems that recommend price.

You won't be starting from zero. We've invested in the foundational data and infrastructure that pricing decisions depend on. What's missing is the capability on top: models the business trusts, experiments that settle pricing questions with evidence, and economics defined once so they hold consistently across Commercial, Product and the customer experience.

The arc of the role runs from measurement to prediction to prescription - understanding how demand responds to price, forecasting how it will respond, and ultimately building the models that recommend the price itself.

What You'll Do: 

- 
Build and own the demand and elasticity modelling capability, quantifying how price affects volume across destination, duration, data tier, and customer segment.

- 
Develop machine learning models for demand forecasting and willingness-to-pay, and take them from exploration through to production with the monitoring and retraining that keeps them honest.

- 
Move us from predictive to prescriptive by building the optimisation layer that turns forecasts and elasticities into recommended prices under margin, competitive and partner constraints.

- 
Design and analyse pricing experiments with statistical rigour, and apply causal methods where clean randomisation isn't possible.

- 
Define pricing within our data ecosystem, owning the governed definitions of price, cost and package economics that reporting, analysis and product surfaces all read from.

- 
Partner with Commercial and Finance to connect pricing decisions to margin and revenue, and to size opportunities before we commit.

- 
Set the analytical standard for pricing at Airalo, from what counts as evidence through to how a model or recommendation gets validated before it influences live pricing.

What You'll Bring: 

- 
7+ years in data science, quantitative economics, or applied research, including pricing, monetisation, or marketplace economics work that demonstrably changed decisions.

- 
Experience with dynamic or algorithmic pricing systems in production.

- 
An advanced degree in Econometrics, Statistics, Operations Research or similar, or equivalent applied depth in demand estimation and the identification problems that make naive price-quantity regressions wrong.

- 
Hands-on machine learning experience across the full lifecycle, from feature engineering and model selection through to deployment

- 
Familiarity with optimisation and decision-science methods that turn predictions into recommended actions, whether through constrained optimisation, bandits, or reinforcement learning approaches.

- 
Proven experimentation expertise, having designed and defended experiments with a clear view on decision frameworks and common failure modes.

- 
Experience building analytical capability where none existed before, turning raw data and a business question into something a commercial team uses repeatedly.

- 
Strong data modelling instincts, thinking in reusable definitions and single sources of truth rather than standalone analyses.

- 
The ability to move comfortably between financial, product and operational data and connect the analysis to a financial outcome.

- 
Genuine partnership instincts, translating between analytical rigour and commercial reality so that Commercial and Product come to you early rather than after the decision.

- 
Fluency in the Python ML stack alongside strong SQL, with the engineering hygiene to hand over code that others can run and maintain.

- 
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to make a methodological argument to people who won't check your standard errors.

- 
A self-starter mindset that thrives in ambiguity and brings structure without waiting for permission.

- 
Comfort using AI tools to augment analytical work, with a point of view on where they help and where they don't

Nice to have: 

- 
Experience in marketplace, telecom, travel, or subscription/usage-based businesses.

- 
Bayesian or hierarchical modelling for sparse segments and long-tail SKUs.

- 
Competitive price response modelling, or working with scraped competitor pricing data.

- 
Familiarity with dbt, LightDash, or similar semantic/BI layers.

- 
Experience designing semantic or metric layers consumed by both analytics and production systems.

- 
Experience working in cross-functional teams spanning commercial, finance and product disciplines.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About Nous 

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

Why we're hiring 

Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it.

Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work.

We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff.

About the role 

You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push.

You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions.

What you'll actually do 

- Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself.

- Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more.

- Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates.

- Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time.

- Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet.

- Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too.

- Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating.

What this role isn't 

- An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job.

- A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more.

- A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked.

- A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes.

- A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above.

What success looks like 

In your first 90 days:

- The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so.

- Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved.

- You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted.

- Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week.

- At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more.

- We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined.

After a year:

- You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to.

- The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well.

- Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you.

- Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings.

About you 

You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something.

You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it.

You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company.

You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise.

AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once.

You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails.

You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does.

You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm.

Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway.

Bonus points:

- You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD.

- You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end.

- You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance).

- You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it.

- You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting.

How you will grow 

This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year.

Remuneration and benefits 

Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

An environment where you can do your best work:

- 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards

- 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier)

- 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally)

- 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine

- ☕ Very good coffee

- 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

- 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

- ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

- 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme

- 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans

Nous has an office-first culture. That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that, sometimes, certain types of work can be better done remotely. Most team members spend 3-4 days a week in the office on average. This role may naturally involve even more presence than that.

The environment 

Most importantly, this is a high-performance, high-agency and high-trust technical environment. Nous is intentionally lean and AI-native, not just in its product but as a company. Everyone is expected to use AI to its full potential, whether that's debugging a system, streamlining a workflow or improving how customers are served. Rather than building layers of middle management, we hire smart, high-agency people and give them real ownership.

We're dedicated to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace, and we actively welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Every candidate is thoughtfully considered, without regard to race, religion, gender expression, disability or sexual orientation.

If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway.

title: Product Manager
description:
About Nous 

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

How we build (worth reading before the role) 

How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next.

We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be.

We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.

About the role 

So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.

You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value.

Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer.

That's also what makes it exciting.

You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together.

Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business.

Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as "product".

Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join.

What matters most 

We need all of these at once:

- Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up.

- Adaptable. We’re working a lot of this out as we go, so the role and the squad will change, probably more than once. You enjoy that. You pick up whatever’s needed, PM work or not, and you work in the open: sharing rough thinking early and changing course when someone has a better idea.

- Delivery. You bring order to a fast-moving squad: clear priorities, sensible sequencing, people unblocked quickly, and an honest look at whether what shipped actually worked.

- Product craft. You find the real problem behind a request and make the trade-offs explicit. You care about the details of what our users actually see.

- Commercial and analytical. You know what your area made last month, what moved it and what you'd do next, and you answer most of your own questions with data. You think in conversion, margin and lifetime value as readily as in features.

- Energy. You've probably worked at a startup. You move fast, you're happy doing the unglamorous work yourself, and you'd rather ship this week's version than polish next quarter's.

And everyone builds here, PMs included. You'll use AI tooling (Claude Code or whatever gets it done) to prototype, dig into data and ship changes yourself. You don't need to be an engineer, but you shouldn't be scared of code.

What you'll actually do 

- Grow your service lines. Understand what really drives their performance, be able to measure it, and lead the squad to deliver it.

- Set the squad's OKRs and roadmap, get the sequencing in place, and drive fast, efficient execution.

- Evaluate what’s being shipped, and own the reporting: make sure the reports and the data behind them make sense.

- Work across product and commercial: the suppliers and tariffs we can offer, the regulation we work within, and what that means for what gets built.

- Run experiments, and unblock yourself on the analysis without always needing an analyst.

- Get close to members and ops. Read the conversations, sit with the people handling the edge cases, and fix the parts of the journey where people drop out or get stuck.

About you 

You'll likely thrive here if:

- You've been a PM for a few years, ideally at a startup, and you've owned something with a number attached: revenue, conversion, retention.

- You've worked on the commercial side as well as the product side: a P&L, a supplier or partner relationship, pricing, or a whole service line.

- You're comfortable enough with data and code to unblock yourself.

Nice-to-haves:

- You were a software engineer before you moved into product.

- You've worked on a transactional or regulated product: insurance, fintech, energy, marketplaces.

- You've built and shipped your own thing: a startup, a side project, an internal tool that took off.

This probably isn't for you if your PM experience is mostly roadmaps and stakeholder management at a big company, with no number you owned.

How we work 

We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. title: Senior Applied Scientist - Behavior AI
description:
The Behavior AI team builds the AI-based anomaly detection behind Datadog's security products. Our models learn what normal looks like across the billions of logs, events, and telemetry records flowing through the platform every second, and they flag the behavior that does not fit, on every record, in real time, at a cost that makes sense at our scale. What we build does not ship to a single feature. The same models power detection across many of Datadog's security products at once, so the work has impact well beyond any one team. Large general-purpose models are too slow and too expensive to run in that path, so we take the opposite approach: small, custom models, designed for high-throughput stream processing and optimized to run cheaply on every record.

We are hiring a Senior Applied Scientist to build these models from start to finish. You will contribute to designing the architecture, training at scale, and the optimization work that takes a model from training to running efficiently on production traffic. This optimization requires a deep understanding of the constraints imposed by both the software and the hardware, together with the applied mathematics to work within them: often it comes down to finding a mathematical reformulation that fits those constraints better, and that judgment can decide whether a model reaches production at all.

The work involves a number of open questions. How do you obtain most of the quality of a large model from one that is far smaller and cheap enough to run on the full stream? Where is it worth trading exactness for speed, and how do you reason about the error you accept? How do you make a small model's outputs clear enough that the detection engineers and analysts who rely on it can trust what it reports? If these are the problems you want to work on, we would like to hear from you.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture: the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. 

What You'll Do: 

- Design and build custom mid-size models for high-throughput stream processing, and train them at scale.

- Optimize these models from start to finish, working across both the mathematics and the systems, often by finding mathematical reformulations that fit the hardware and software constraints better.

- Build the training data pipelines the work depends on when they do not already exist, from the raw stream to a training-ready dataset.

- Work with engineering to integrate models into production, with a clear focus on GPU utilization, latency, and cost per record on live traffic.

- Plan the roadmap of model and system improvements, based on a solid understanding of the product and of what matters most to users.

- Build an agentic layer on top of the models to analyze, validate, and act on their outputs.

- Build lightweight interpretability tools that make model behavior easier to explain to the people who rely on it.

- Maintain and monitor the models, services, and infrastructure your team owns, and take part in your team's on-call rotation.

title: Senior Applied Scientist - AI Platform
description:
AI Platform builds the foundations of Datadog's AI efforts. The org is 70+ people organised in three pillars: training and serving (GPU clusters, distributed training, low-level infrastructure), agents (agent harnesses, memory systems, the internal AI gateway that routes every LLM request at Datadog), and evaluation and experimentation. This role sits in the evaluation and experimentation pillar, which owns Datadog's shared annotation and evaluation infrastructure — including the evaluation scenario store and the telemetry archival systems used across the Bits org. Together they let an agent travel back in time and query what Datadog looked like at the exact moment an incident happened, so scenarios can be replayed and agent performance tracked over time.

Specifically, you'll be the first applied scientist on GenSim (Generative Simulations), the team that builds the environments Datadog's agents learn in. GenSim doesn't replay sampled telemetry — it stands up real, fully instrumented applications that talk to Datadog, drives them with representative traffic, injects controlled failures, and records what happens. Because GenSim injected the failure, it knows the ground truth. That corpus — hundreds of postmortem-derived scenarios and thousands of runnable applications — is today the primary source of post-training data for Datadog's own SRE model, and the substrate that Bits AI SRE and our other agents are trained and evaluated against.

The team has no applied science support today and is learning post-training data methodology on the fly. That's the gap this role fills, and the open questions are the interesting part. How do you tell whether a generated environment is actually representative of the messy, incomplete telemetry real customers run — rather than a suspiciously clean one where every monitor exists and every service emits complete logs? How do you make injected problems genuinely hard, and how do you even measure difficulty? How do you define and control the quality of post-training data when correctness, representativeness and difficulty pull in different directions? How do you evaluate an agent end to end when the trajectory is non-deterministic? Creating simulated agent environments for monitoring and SRE work is not well solved in open source or in published research, and Datadog is the leading company in this field. If those are the problems you want to spend your time on, come build this with us.

What You'll Do: 

- Own the applied science direction for GenSim: set the methodology and the forward-looking technical calls on how simulated environments and post-training data should be built, on a team where that decision-making does not exist yet.

- Define, measure and raise the quality of post-training data — basic correctness, representativeness against the real distribution of customer systems and production telemetry, and difficulty — and make those measures something the team can act on release over release.

- Close the realism gap. Simulated environments today are too clean and the injected problems are not yet hard enough; you'll drive the research and the engineering that make them look like real, imperfect production systems.

- Build scalable, production-grade systems rather than research scripts. The output is not just a dataset — it is a system of synthetic environments that must be reliable and invokable inside a training loop.

- Determine how this data is best applied, in LLM post-training and in evaluation, and own the agent and LLM application evaluation approaches for these environments.

- Work cross-functionally with the engineers and applied scientists on adjacent teams — Bits AI SRE, the model training effort, and the wider evaluation and experimentation pillar — so that what you learn moves freely in both directions.

Who You Are: 

- You have a PhD, MS or equivalent research experience in a scientific field, with strong applied mathematics grounding.

- 6+ years of relevant applied science or ML engineering experience, including setting technical direction for others.

- You have hands-on experience with LLM and agent post-training data: how it is created, managed, and how training-data quality is controlled. This is the requirement that matters most.

- You have real domain expertise in LLMs and agentic applications — not classical ML fine-tuning. Fine-tuning classifiers or traditional models is a different problem from the one this team is solving.

- You have evaluated agents or LLM applications, and can define what 'good' means before you measure it.

- You are a strong programmer and production software engineer. Python at minimum, plus the ability to ship scalable production systems and work with distributed systems.

- You collaborate well across engineering and science teams, and you're comfortable being the domain expert who decides what comes next.

- You thrive in ambiguity and can make sound technical calls when the path isn't yet defined.

Bonus Points: 

- Hands-on LLM fine-tuning, post-training or model training experience.

- Background in statistics, experiment design and data analysis.

- Experience deploying production-level ML infrastructure.

- Architecture-level understanding of LLMs.

title: AI Research Engineer - Datadog AI Research (DAIR)
description:
As a Research Engineer on our team, you will partner with Research Scientists to turn research ideas into working systems, building the data, tooling, and infrastructure that enable rapid iteration, trustworthy evaluation, and a smooth path from prototype to production.

Building on our track record of AI-powered solutions (e.g., Bits AI , Bits Evolve , and our time series foundation model ), Datadog AI Research tackles high-risk, high-reward problems grounded in real-world challenges in cloud observability and security.

We are focused on two research areas:

- World Models for Observability -- Training multimodal foundation models that learn the joint dynamics of distributed systems across metrics, traces, logs, topology, and events. These models power advanced forecasting, anomaly detection, root cause analysis, counterfactual simulation ("what if?"), and provide a learned planning backbone for our autonomous agents.

- Trained Agents for Observability -- Post-training models to operate autonomously across Datadog's domain. SRE incident response is our first target, with a clear path to code repair, security response, and infrastructure optimization. We build the simulation environments, RL training loops, and evaluation infrastructure needed to train agents that match or surpass frontier models at a fraction of the cost.

What You'll Do: 

- Build and operate multimodal data pipelines, training and evaluation infrastructure, benchmarks, and internal tooling

- Implement models, run experiments at scale, and profile for reliability, performance, and cost

- Build simulation environments and replay infrastructure for agent training and evaluation

- Orchestrate distributed training and distributed RL with Ray, including scheduling, scaling, and failure recovery

- Establish rigorous automated benchmarks and regression tests for world model predictions, agent performance, and simulation fidelity

- Collaborate with Research Scientists, Product, and Engineering to integrate capabilities into Datadog's products and to harden prototypes into reliable services

- Contribute to research publications at top-tier conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML), and produce high-quality code, documentation, and open-source artifacts

Who You Are: 

- You have depth in distributed computing, RL Infra, and ML systems for training and inference at scale; experience with Ray, Slurm, or similar frameworks is a plus

- You are proficient in Python, familiar with a systems language (e.g., Rust, C++, or Go), and comfortable with modern cloud and data infrastructure

- You have practical experience implementing and operating ML training and inference systems (e.g., PyTorch or JAX), including containerization, orchestration, and GPU acceleration

- You have practical experience with large-scale model training and fine-tuning, including frameworks like Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, SkyRL, VeRL, or TorchTitan, and techniques such as SFT, RLVR, RLHF, and efficient inference (quantization, speculative decoding)

- You can explain design and performance trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences

- You have experience supporting or contributing to research publications

Bonus Points (any of the following): 

- You have strong software engineering skills with experience in domains such as observability, SRE, or security

- You have experience bridging research prototypes and real-world product applications, especially with large foundation models, world models, or RL-trained agents

- You have a passion for pushing the boundaries of AI with a focus on customer impact and scalable deployment

- You have hands-on experience with GPU programming and optimization, including CUDA

- You have experience writing production data pipelines and applications

- You have experience building simulation or sandbox environments for agent training

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

- Opportunity to attend and present at conferences and meetups

As a Deployment Strategist, you are the owner of the customer's problem and the value we promise to deliver. You will work with senior customer stakeholders to scope value, define pilots and releases, steer delivery through to go-live, and drive adoption so that value is actually realized after launch. You combine the discipline of a program manager with the product thinking of a field product owner, and you are as comfortable in a steering committee as you are in a working session with plant engineers.

This is a hands-on role. You are expected to shape the engagement, not just report on it.

What You'll Do 

Scope and define value

Own delivery outcomes

- Manage risk, dependencies, and escalations across customer, partner, and internal teams, and unblock technical and political issues early.

- Own delivery health: plan, margin, forecast, resourcing needs, and status reporting.

Drive adoption and value realization 

- Own the path from go-live to measurable usage: adoption plans, enablement and training, user feedback loops, and health indicators.

Lead with partners and the team

- Guide Solution Architects, Data Engineers, and Data Scientists in the engagement, and coach junior colleagues.

- Contribute to the Value Delivery playbook: lessons learned, reusable templates, and delivery standards.

Feed the product

- Use AI tooling in your own work (analysis, documentation, reporting, prototyping) and help the team raise its standard.

Must have 

- 5+ years of experience in customer-facing delivery, program management or technical advisory for enterprise software or data/AI platforms.

- A track record of owning complex, ambiguous engagements through to measurable customer outcomes.

- Executive-level communication: you can present, negotiate, and make decisions with senior customer stakeholders and with delivery engineers on the same day.

- Strong command of agile and iterative delivery, backlog prioritisation, and scope management.

- Exposure to industrial data, knowledge graphs, or operational technology environments.

title: Acoustic Researcher
description:
Full-time · On-site (Paris Marseille) 

The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer.

Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. It will be deployed on a distributed, autonomous network of vectors (UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys, seabed…) to provide real-time understanding of underwater threats.

France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service.

Pelagon is backed by Hexa , the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised.

Why this matters 

The sea is the physical layer of the economy — and Europe's most exposed flank. Everything that moves beneath the surface leaves an acoustic trace, but the ocean is a brutal channel: multipath, ambient noise, shifting propagation. Reading it is first and foremost a physics problem.

France and Europe have a world-class heritage in underwater acoustics and sonar. Pelagon's bet is to bridge that science with modern physical-AI strategies and a distributed fleet of UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys and seabed sensors. As our Acoustic Researcher , you are the physics backbone of that system — the person who understands underwater sound deeply enough that our models can learn from it. You partner directly with our AI Engineers, who consume the features, representations and data you help define.

What you'll do 

- Model underwater sound propagation across realistic ocean environments to enable our synthetic data generation pipeline.

- Characterize and classify acoustic signatures of surface and underwater targets; build the ground-truth understanding our multimodal acoustic model is trained against.

- Design and reason about sensor and array geometries: what to deploy, where, and how to extract maximum information from constrained & distributed vectors.

- Work hand in hand with AI Engineers on physics-constrained learning strategies ans models.

What we look for 

- Deep grounding in underwater acoustics, sonar, or a closely related field (ocean acoustics, radar/array processing, acoustic signal processing). PhD or equivalent research experience.

- Strong command of statistical signal processing: detection & estimation theory, array processing, time-frequency analysis.

- Fluent in Python (NumPy/SciPy) for modeling, simulation and analysis; comfortable working with large datasets.

- A builder's instinct, you want your work deployed at sea, not left in a paper. Bias toward validating ideas against real data.

- Bonus: prior experience using machine learning on acoustic signals, naval / defense domain experience.

Why join now 

- Founding ownership. You'll be one of the first engineers and will define the technical foundation of the company. Meaningful equity comes with that.

- A mission with weight. This is hardware that protects critical infrastructure and Europe's maritime space.

- Real things, in the real ocean, fast. You'll see your work in the water within weeks, not years.

- AI-first, at the edge, in the real world. We train our own models and run them where it counts: in the water, on the device. You'll be solving the edge-ML and power problems most companies only talk about.

- A sovereign, European deeptech at the inflection point of a market with strong NATO and EU policy momentum behind it.

Founded in 2025 by Lydia Bellahouel (CEO) and Camille Epitalon (CTO), Verso is backed by Hexa (eFounders), the pioneer European startup studio behind 40+ companies including Front, Aircall and Spendesk.

Consumer research has been slow and expensive for decades. We are building the company that changes that, and we need our first commercial hire: the person who brings our product to enterprise customers, closes our first flagship accounts, and helps define how Verso sells.

About Verso and who we are

Verso is an AI-native consumer research platform. Our AI designs the study, interviews real participants one to one over video in any language, and turns those conversations into a structured, evidence-backed report you can interrogate in chat. Days instead of weeks, at a fraction of the cost of a traditional agency, without trading rigor for speed.

We sell to insights, marketing and innovation teams at global brands, with a strong pull from large CPG, beauty, telecom, retail, and the strategy consultancies that serve them. Early clients include Orange, Michelin, Europcar and dsm-firmenich. We are a small team with high standards and one clear thesis: qualitative research is high-signal and badly broken, and AI is finally good enough to fix it.

We start with AI-moderated qualitative research and are building for each client a system of consumer intelligence: every study compounds into a living understanding of their consumers that their teams, and their own AI, can draw on over time.

Lydia spent 7 years at BCG leading AI-powered transformation for consumer brands and knows the buyer's pain from the inside. Camille is an AI expert and a pioneer in agentic systems. Together they built Verso to turn consumer understanding into a real-time advantage for the brands we serve.

The role

We are hiring our Head of Sales, the first dedicated commercial hire at Verso.

This is a hands-on, full-cycle role, and you work hand in hand with the founders, Lydia in particular, who leads commercial today. You prospect, run demos, scope pilots, and close enterprise contracts yourself. As we grow, you help define how Verso sells and have the opportunity to build and lead the commercial team.

To be clear on the shape of it: you close deals now, and you grow into running the function next. This is not a co-founder seat, it is the first commercial hire, with real room to make the role your own. If you want the leadership part without the selling part, this is not it.

- The sales process itself. You turn founder-led selling into something repeatable: the motion, the collateral, the CRM discipline, the qualification bar, the pricing conversation. You decide what good looks like and write it down so the next hire can run it.

- Enterprise relationships. Our buyers are Heads of Insights and research leaders who buy on trust, not on a feature list. You build that trust, turn a first pilot into an annual program, and grow accounts study by study.

- AI-driven selling. You use AI across your own workflow, from research and prospecting to follow-ups and proposals, and you sell a product that is itself AI-native. You are fluent enough to demo it credibly and to make the "rigor, not hype" case to a skeptical researcher.

- Voice of the customer. You are closest to the market and bring structured feedback to the founders, helping shape what we build next.

Who you are

- You have 5+ years of experience in enterprise B2B sales and have personally closed complex, consultative deals. You know how to navigate long, multi-stakeholder buying cycles and turn initial projects into long-term customer relationships.

- You run the full cycle without a playbook handed to you, and you are comfortable being the person who writes it.

This role is for you if

- You like closing deals yourself and you want the path from there to leading the function.

- You need a team under you on day one rather than earning it.

title: Feed System Functional Engineer
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

You will own the functional architecture and performance of the propellant feed system for a storable bipropellant propulsion system (MON3-MMH system). You will be responsible for ensuring the feed system delivers propellants to the thrusters within required specifications across the full mission envelope — from ground fill through operation, and recovery.

Role Overview

System Architecture

- Define and maintain the functional architecture of the feed system including propellant tanks, lines, valves, filters, thrusters and instrumentation.

- Perform system-level sizing, sensitivity analyses and functional simulations

System Development

- Define functional requirements for subsystems based on propellant system analyses

- Identify key verification and validation steps required at the system and subsystem level to demonstrate compliance with specification

Modeling & Analysis

- Develop and maintain fluid system models (steady-state and transient) to predict pressure drop, flow rates, water hammer, thruster cross-coupling, and priming behavior.

- Verify compliance between system nominal and off-nominal operation with subsystem operational domains (such as thruster envelope).

- Analyze failure modes (leakage, contamination, cavitation, fluid hammer) and define mitigation strategies and design margins.

Verification & Test

- Lead functional and performance verification: cold-flow, functional and hot-fire tests from component to assembly level .

- Correlate test data against predictive models and update margins/requirements accordingly.

Integration Support

- Support integration, qualification, and operations reviews (design reviews, FMEA, test readiness reviews).

- Interface across design, test, and operations functions throughout the vehicle lifecycle.

You will perform your duties principally at the Company's premises in Bordeaux and may be required to travel from time to time to our company’s premises in Munich in the course of your duties.

What we would love to see from you

- Master’s and/or PhD degree in Aerospace Engineering or a related field

- Proven experience with python and 0D - 1D fluid simulation tools (model development and analyses) - (e.g., EcosimPro or equivalent)

- Hands-on experience in propulsion system design for launch vehicles, spacecraft, or space capsules, with direct exposure to liquid propulsion architectures.

title: Legal Counsel
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 

About the role 

You are BLP's first in-house lawyer. You build the legal function from scratch and protect a business that puts agentic AI into the ERP processes of 550+ enterprise customers. You report to the CFO and partner closely with Sales, Finance, People and Product, covering four entities in Switzerland, Germany, the UK and the US, with customers in 40+ countries. In your first 12 months, Sales runs on your contract playbook and standard templates, and BLP has a clear compliance framework for data protection and AI regulation.

What you'll do 

· Own commercial contracting end-to-end: negotiate customer MSAs, DPAs and SLAs with enterprise procurement and legal teams, so deals close faster with risk you can explain to the CFO.

· Build the legal toolkit: templates, a negotiation playbook with fallback positions and clear approval rules, so Sales can handle standard deals without escalating to you.

· Lead data protection and AI compliance across GDPR, the Swiss FADP and the EU AI Act, and support security reviews and certifications, so enterprise customers trust how we handle their data.

· Run corporate housekeeping for BLP Digital AG and its subsidiaries in Germany, the UK and the US: board and shareholder matters and cap table

· Advise on employment law across our countries and protect our IP and trademarks, working with the People team on contracts, policies and equity plans.

· Select and manage external counsel, deciding what stays in-house and what goes out.

What you'll bring 

· You bring 7+ years of legal experience, including at least 3 years in-house at a B2B SaaS or tech company, ideally after training at a leading law firm.

· You are admitted to the bar in Switzerland or another European jurisdiction and are comfortable advising on Swiss, EU, UK and US matters with appropriate external support.

· You have personally negotiated enterprise SaaS contracts with large corporate customers and closed them on terms the business could live with.

· You have hands-on GDPR and data protection experience and follow the EU AI Act closely.

· You have built something from zero before: a template library, a contract process or a legal function, and you are happy to be the only lawyer in the room.

· You are pragmatic and commercial in your approach. You give clear, risk-weighted advice in plain language, at the speed of a fast-growing company, in fluent English and German language.

Strong plus 

· Experience with venture financing rounds, ESOP setups and/or M&A.

· Background in ERP, finance automation or AI products.

· Experience with ISO 27001 or SOC 2 audits from the legal side.

What you'll get 

· Founding ownership. You shape BLP's legal function from day one and decide how it scales.

· Direct line to leadership. You report directly to the CFO and work with the leadership team on decisions that matter.

· Global scope. Four entities, 40+ countries and enterprise customers give you breadth few in-house roles offer.

· You work at the front line of AI regulation, applied to real enterprise processes.

· You grow with the company and are set up to build and lead a team as legal needs expand.

· You work from our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, with a team that values Impact, Transparency, Ownership and Excellence.

· Competitive package. 

Learn more about BLP and our values at blp.digital/company/careers .

title: Strategic Account Executive (Zurich)
description:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

ROLE OVERVIEW 

We are seeking a motivated and results-driven Strategic Account Executive to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for driving new business within your territory, focusing on building and maintaining strong relationships with key stakeholders across various personas within an account. You will play a crucial role in expanding our customer base and ensuring successful sales outcomes through effective pipeline generation and accurate sales forecasting.

- Pipeline Generation: Creating 80% of your pipeline by identifying new business opportunities and engaging with multiple personas within the prospect/customer base. Utilize various strategies and tools to generate leads and move them through the sales cycle.

- Sales Forecasting: Develop and maintain accurate sales forecasts (+/- 10 of goal), leveraging data to inform decision-making and ensure predictable revenue outcomes with the goal of consistent attainment of revenue targets.

- Solution Selling: Effectively communicate the value of our platform, tailoring presentations and proposals to meet the specific needs of each prospect.

- Negotiation and Closing: Lead negotiations with potential clients, by thoughtfully addressing key stakeholders including multiple personas and CxO in the buyer journey, while navigating organizational complexities, addressing objections and securing new business agreements.

- Account Management: Work across multiple personas within an account to understand their unique needs and align Benchling’s solutions with their business objectives.

- Collaboration: Partner with internal teams (marketing, product, customer success, etc) and Channel to ensure a seamless experience for clients and drive long-term customer satisfaction.

- Continuous Learning: Stay informed about industry trends, competitors, and emerging technologies to maintain a competitive edge in the market.

- Process: Drive the sales process through Pipeline Generation (PG), 3 Why’s, Champion Building, MEDDICC, Command of the Message, etc. Maintain account integrity and opportunity data within company systems; Salesforce.

QUALIFICATIONS 

You are drawn to our mission and you want to help Benchling win new business. You are committed to working in a collaborative environment, working together as a team. You have a love for working in a fast-paced environment and taking the initiative to get stuff done and try new things. You are passionate about powering new possibilities in biotech faster.

- Proven experience as an Account Executive, preferably within a data management, workflow SaaS or technology-driven environment that sells to multiple personas across IT & Line of business.

- Demonstrated ability to drive pipeline generation and manage complex sales cycles.

- Strong sales forecasting skills with a track record of meeting or exceeding targets.

- Demonstrated success in selling products or solutions that typically fall outside of pre-established budgets, with a proven ability to build a compelling business case and influence purchasing decisions.

- Experience working with diverse personas within an account (from technical decision makers, business decision makers & CxO execs), with the ability to influence decision-making at all the levels.

- Dynamic communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.

- Self-motivated, with a strong drive to achieve and exceed goals.

- Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team environment.

- Familiarity with MEDDICC sales methodology is a plus but not required.

- Knowledge of the life sciences industry, including: R&D, and/or IT functions is preferred but not required.

- Bachelor’s degree - life sciences major is preferred but not required.

HOW WE WORK

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

title: Senior Specialist, QA
description:
About Summit: 

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company with a mission focused on improving quality of life, increasing potential duration of life, and resolving serious unmet medical needs. At Summit, we believe in building a team of world class professionals who are passionate about this mission, and it is our people who drive this mission to reality. Summit’s core values include integrity, passion for excellence, purposeful urgency, collaboration, and our commitment to people. Our employees are truly the heart and soul of our culture, and they are invaluable in shaping our journey toward excellence.

Summit’s team is inspired to touch and help change lives through Summit’s clinical studies in the field of oncology. Summit has multiple global Phase 3 clinical studies, including:

Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) 

- 
HARMONi: Phase 3 clinical study which was intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a 3rd generation EGFR TKI.

- 
HARMONi-3: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

- 
HARMONi-7: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

Colorectal Cancer (CRC) 

- 
HARMONi-GI3: Phase 3 clinical study intended to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy not presently approved by any regulatory authority other than China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, and has additional offices in California, New Jersey, the UK, and Ireland. 

Overview of Role: 

The Senior Specialist, QA will provide operational leadership and quality oversight for the review, approval and release-readiness of clinical and commercial product batches. 

The role is responsible for ensuring that batch documentation is complete, accurate, traceable, and compliant with applicable GMP requirements, approved procedures and regulatory commitments before submission to QA for final disposition or QP certification. The person will coordinate batch-release activities across Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs and external manufacturing partners, ensuring that issues are identified, escalated and resolved in a timely manner. The position will also lead process improvements, support inspection readiness and promote high standards of data integrity and Good Documentation Practice across the batch-release process. 

Key Responsibilities 

- Batch Review and Release Readiness 

- Coordinate the end-to-end QA review of executed batch manufacturing, packaging, testing and release documentation for IMP and Commercial biological batch records. 

- Coordinate the preparation and collation of batch documentation required for final batch disposition or QP certification from internal and external sources. 

- Verify that batch records are complete, accurate, and compliant with approved procedures, specifications and applicable GMP requirements. 

- Confirm that relevant deviations, investigations, change controls, CAPAs, and laboratory results have been appropriately assessed and approved before release. 

- Identify documentation gaps, discrepancies and potential compliance risks, and coordinate their timely resolution. 

- Maintain oversight of batch-release priorities, review status, outstanding actions, and planned release dates. 

- Escalate critical issues or potential delays to Quality leadership and relevant stakeholders. 

- Ensure that batch-release documentation is appropriately archived and readily retrievable electronically. 

- Quality Systems and Compliance: 

- Ensure batch-release activities are performed in accordance with current GMP, Good Documentation Practice, data-integrity principles, and internal procedures. 

- Support the effective operation of quality systems associated with deviations, CAPAs, change controls, document control, and training. 

- Review and approve relevant quality documents, including SOPs, work instructions, forms, checklists, and batch-release procedures. 

- Maintain controlled documentation and ensure that current approved versions are available to relevant personnel. 

- Support periodic reviews of procedures and identify opportunities to strengthen compliance and operational effectiveness. 

- Promote the appropriate use of electronic quality and document management systems. 

- Act as a subject-matter expert for batch documentation, release-readiness and associated document-control processes for all batch release activities. 

- Internal Team Coordination (EU QA) 

- Provide day-to-day leadership and technical guidance to QA batch reviewers and supporting personnel. 

- Plan and allocate batch-review activities according to business priorities, product demand, and release timelines. 

- Monitor team workload, quality metrics, and completion of assigned activities. 

- Develop and deliver training in Good Documentation Practice, batch-record review and relevant quality-system processes. 

- Support onboarding and qualifications of new QA team members. 

- Foster a collaborative, accountable, and continuous-improvement culture within the QA function. 

- External Team Collaboration: 

- Work closely with Manufacturing, Quality Control / CMC, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Supply and other relevant functions to support timely batch release. 

- Coordinate with all Summit CMOs, testing laboratories and service providers to obtain missing documents and resolve release-related queries. 

- Communicate batch status, risks, priorities and outstanding actions clearly to internal and external stakeholders. 

- Support changes affecting batch documentation or release processes. 

- Participate in cross-functional meetings concerning batch disposition, documentation, readiness, and supply continuity internally. 

- Inspection Readiness and Continuous Improvement 

- Maintain batch-release processes and supporting records in a continuous state of inspection of readiness. 

- Support regulatory inspections, customer audits, internal audits, and supplier audits. 

- Retrieve and present batch documentation and quality-system records during audits and inspections. 

- Track batch-review metrics, recurring documentation issues, cycle times, and overdue actions. 

- Analyse trends and recommend improvements to increase efficiency, right-first-time performance and compliance. 

- Lead or contribute to Lean and process-optimization initiatives within the batch-release function. 

- Support the implementation and enhancement of electronic quality, document management and reporting systems. 

Qualifications and Experience 

- Essential 

- Recognized qualification in Quality, Pharmaceutical Science, Life Sciences, Engineering or related discipline. 

- Significant experience in Quality Assurance within a pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical or similarly regulated manufacturing environment – preferably in Biologic manufacturing, Packaging and Labelling environments. 

- Practical experience reviewing executed batch records and supporting batch disposition or QP certification activities. 

- Knowledge of GMP, Good Documentation Practice, and data-integrity requirements. 

- Experience working with deviations, investigations, CAPAs, and change controls. 

- Experience using electronic quality, document management and other enterprise-systems - systems such as MasterControl, NetSuite, Veeva Vault, TrackWise, SAP or equivalent platforms. 

- Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple priorities and deliver against critical release timelines. 

- Experience supporting the release of medicinal products or investigational medicinal products. 

- Experience working with contract manufacturing organizations and external testing laboratories 

- Key Competencies 

- Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy
